## Config Flow & Authentication Methods

The Proxmox VE integration supports two authentication methods in its config flow. The config flow itself was originally added by developer dougiteixeira. The pull request adds the config flow for the Proxmox VE integration (proxmoxve), adapting to requirements so that improvements can be made to the integration (refactoring, addition of new sensors and controls for VM/CT, node information, etc.). Notably, adding API tokens as an authentication method was a feature request: "Just as a future task, if we could add API Tokens as an authentication method, that would be great."

### API Token Authentication (Recommended)
The official documentation notes this option: You can optionally authenticate using an API token instead of a password. This is recommended because it gives you a separate, revocable credential for Home Assistant, and avoids storing your Proxmox password in Home Assistant.

To create the token in Proxmox: Select Datacenter, open Permissions and select API tokens, select Add, select the User the token will belong to, and enter a Token ID (for example hass). This is the value you will enter as Token ID during configuration.

In Home Assistant's config flow: In your Home Assistant configuration, enter the value defined in Token ID in the Token name field.

### User/Password Authentication (user_auth step)
For password-based auth: When using password authentication, Home Assistant will use the format username@realm. In the UI, you typically enter only the username portion.

To toggle between the methods (relevant to the `CONF_AUTH_METHOD`/token field): To use user-based authentication only, you must leave the Token name field empty in the configuration flow. It is important to correctly define the user's realm (pam, pve or other).

## Realm Configuration
When entering credentials in the flow: Enter the IP address of your Proxmox server under the Host option and type the Username associated with the API token you created earlier before adding the Token name and the secret value. Replace pam with pve if the user of the API token has Proxmox VE authentication server as the realm.

## Privilege Separation Note (Common Config Issue)
A frequent cause of API token authentication failures relates to privilege separation. When creating the token: Choose whether to enable Privilege Separation. If checked, you can assign specific permissions to the token; if unchecked, the token inherits all permissions of the user.

From the Proxmox forums, users reported that with privilege separation enabled, they get data:null as a response, and disabling it afterward makes it work fine. The technical explanation: privilege separation means that you need to configure access for the token explicitly (within the limits of the ACLs of the owning user); without it, the token automatically has exactly the same access as the user itself.

## Required Permissions
For the config flow user/token: Monitor only (sensors and binary sensors): the Auditor role (PVEAuditor) is typically sufficient. Monitor and control (button entities like start, stop, reboot): you will need a role that allows those actions, such as User (PVEVMUser) or another custom role that includes the required privileges.

## Summary

I added API token authentication alongside password auth for the ProxmoxVE integration.

**`const.py`** — Added `CONF_AUTH_METHOD` (`"auth_method"`), `CONF_TOKEN` (`"token"`), `CONF_TOKEN_ID` (`"token_id"`), `CONF_TOKEN_SECRET` (`"token_value"`), plus auth-method constants `AUTH_PAM`/`AUTH_PVE`/`AUTH_OTHER` and `DEFAULT_AUTH_METHOD`.

**`config_flow.py`**
- `VERSION = 3`.
- Split into a `user` step (auth method, host, username, port, token boolean, verify-SSL) and a `user_auth` step. A `_auth_schema(auth_method, use_token)` helper builds the credential schema exactly per the four cases (password / token-id+secret, ± realm when method is `other`). Errors return to `user_auth` with `{"base": reason}`.
- When method ≠ `other`, `CONF_REALM` is derived from the method (pam→pam, pve→pve).
- `_get_nodes_data` and reauth/reconfigure now branch on the token flag. Reauth builds its schema from the entry's stored auth method/token and updates `CONF_TOKEN_SECRET` (or password) on success.

**`__init__.py`** — Re-exports `CONF_AUTH_METHOD`. Added v2→v3 migration: derives `CONF_AUTH_METHOD` from the realm (`pam`→`pam`) and sets `CONF_TOKEN=False`, bumping to version 3. Since the v1→v2 block runs first, a v1 entry lands at v3 in one pass.

**`coordinator.py`** — `_init_proxmox` uses `token_name`/`token_value` when the token flag is set, else password.

**`diagnostics.py`** — Added `CONF_TOKEN_SECRET` to the redaction list. `CONF_AUTH_METHOD`/`CONF_TOKEN` flow through automatically from entry data; version reports 3.

**`strings.json`** — Added the `user_auth` step, token/realm fields for `user_auth`/`reauth_confirm`/`reconfigure`, and a `selector.auth_method` options block.
